item.title: The State as a Private Bank Account
item.description: When politics and big business come together: The example of Andrej Babiš shows how a head of government can use political power and state subsidies to benefit his own businesses. Five warning signs show how kleptocracy develops—and why this is not just a problem in the Czech Republic.

item.title: Hack Exposes Inner Workings of Russian Influence Operation „Storm-1516“
item.description:
John Mark Dougan, a U.S. citizen, is considered the architect of „Storm-1516“, one of Russia’s most effective disinformation campaigns. A hack of his systems that CORRECTIV and The Insider examined contains evidence of his activities and funding by a Russian think tank with ties to the government.

The post Hack Exposes Inner Workings of Russian Influence Operation „Storm-1516“ appeared first on correctiv.org.

item.title: How we invented the Pancake Index
item.description:
CORRECTIV’s Pancake Index compares the affordability of four staple ingredients across Europe. Read the full methodology here.

The post How we invented the Pancake Index appeared first on correctiv.org.

item.title: Pancake Index
item.description:
Milk, Flour, Eggs: Rising prices for basic foods are putting pressure on households across Europe. Has it become more or less affordable for you to make simple pancakes? Find out with our interactive tool – and compare with other countries.

The post Pancake Index appeared first on correctiv.org.

item.title: Disaster Preparedness in Germany: In an Emergency, Where You Live Matters
item.description:
Disaster Preparedness in Germany: In an Emergency, Where You Live Matters Is Germany prepared for blackouts, floods, and war? A nationwide investigation by CORRECTIV reveals that crisis plans, funding, and personnel are often lacking. How well people are protected also depends on where they live. How well people are protected in a crisis depends heavily […]

The post Disaster Preparedness in Germany: In an Emergency, Where You Live Matters appeared first on correctiv.org.

item.title: Disaster Strikes – Then What? Gaps in Local Crisis Preparedness
item.description: How well people are protected during a crisis depends heavily on where in Germany they live. This is according to the results of a questionnaire prepared by CORRECTIV and distributed among all 401 counties and independent cities in Germany.

item.title: First the Broadcaster: Why Autocrats Target Broadcasting
item.description: In the Saxony-Anhalt state election, the AfD secured 43.8 percent of the vote, and their first pledge is to terminate the state broadcasting treaties. Why do authoritarian parties target public service broadcasting first? In her native Slovakia, our author witnessed how a broadcaster was hollowed out within 18 months, without anyone having to storm the newsroom. A look at Hungary, Poland, and Italy reveals a recurring playbook behind this and what Germany can learn from it.

item.title: The Tradwife: The Kitchen Is the Front Line
item.description: In authoritarian regimes, the “tradwife” trend is more than just a social media aesthetic: Behind the idyllic family scenes and dough-kneading lies a low-cost propaganda strategy that portrays submission as a free choice.

item.title: Terrorizing the Indigenous: Russian Repression Against Its Own Nations
item.description: Russia’s Indigenous communities live on territories rich in oil, gas, and other natural resources, but their legal power to protect those lands has steadily disappeared. Those who resist industrial expansion and defend Indigenous rights are increasingly treated as threats to state security.

item.title: What we miss when we say “the Kurds”
item.description: Kurdish identity is often treated as one thing. In reality, like many other national and ethnic identities, it is shaped by borders, languages, religions, regions, parties, memories and competing political dreams.

item.title: Pesticides, Mercury, Lead: How Clean is Your Bathing Site Really?
item.description: Officially, most bathing sites are designated as clean. However, research by CORRECTIV.Europe indicates that bathing waters at thousands of sites across Europe are contaminated with chemical pollutants – in some cases posing health risks.

item.title: The Ideal Woman: How autocrats built the archetype.
item.description: Women in autocracies often seem like the regime’s showcase figures. Whether it is patriotic breast implants or pastel dresses as a sign of evangelical modesty, their appearance conveys political messages that can hardly be stated openly. A text about female power in the service of unfreedom.

item.title: Nowhere to Exist: Queer and Trans Afghans on The Move
item.description: An Escape is meant to bring people from danger to safety. For queer and trans Afghans, however, it does not. Instead, it leads them from Taliban rule to familial control, to regional deportation regimes, to bureaucratic indifference—a chain without any moment of arrival.

item.title: Discover How Drought is Affecting your Region
item.description: An analysis by CORRECTIV.Europe reveals for the first time how widespread drought has become across Europe. Two-thirds of all regions have recorded severe drought years since 2012.

item.title: Made in Moscow: The Foreign Agent Law as a Blueprint for Autocrats
item.description: It is not a secret weapon or a military tactic. It is a law — bureaucratic, dull, and devastatingly effective. Russia’s 2012 foreign agent legislation gave autocrats everywhere a template for dismantling civil society while keeping their hands seemingly clean.

item.title: “They protect the law while breaking it”: Inside Europol’s Shadow IT System
item.description: Europol is aiming to become a powerful police force with far-reaching surveillance powers. But in an attempt to deliver in the fight against serious cross-border crime, the agency has apparently gone rogue itself, this investigation reveals: Secret data analysis platforms have put innocent citizens at risk, an issue that remains unresolved today.

item.title: A Ukrainian in a Russian Uniform
item.description: What prisoners of war from the occupied territories reveal about identity, coercion, and the story Russia tells about why it went to war - and why it matters for how Europe understands Russia's justification for the war.

item.title: Half of Europe’s towns and villages have fewer residents than 60 years ago
item.description:
A data analysis by CORRECTIV.Europe reveals for the first time that even as Europe’s overall population grows, half of its municipalities are losing inhabitants – putting increasing pressure on the quality of life in rural areas.

The post Half of Europe’s towns and villages have fewer residents than 60 years ago appeared first on correctiv.org.

item.title: Signal Phishing Attack: Digital Evidence Points to Russia
item.description: For weeks, a wave of attacks has been targeting Signal users in Germany and abroad. Among those targeted are security officials, politicians, and journalists. A CORRECTIV investigation found digital evidence pointing to Russian involvement in the campaign – and a connection to previous attacks in Ukraine and Moldova.

item.title: Housing Cost: One in Seven Municipalities in Europe Unaffordable for Nurses
item.description: Data analysis by CORRECTIV.Europe reveals: In these European locations, even a mid-level salary like a nurse's is not enough to afford a small apartment.

item.title: The New German War Machine
item.description: Germany’s transformation into a military power is in full swing: confidential government documents reveal plans to channel billions into ammunition and controversial weapons systems. Is the country prepared for the consequences?

item.title: The Oligarch-Autocrat Alliances
item.description: Democracy is not dying by sudden coup – it is being dismantled through the law itself, using a shared playbook refined across continents.

item.title: Learning to Backslide: How Autocrats Share Money, Methods, and Models
item.description: Democracy is not dying by sudden coup – it is being dismantled through the law itself, using a shared playbook refined across continents.

item.title: Azerbaijan: The Price of Victory and the Silence of Dissent
item.description: In this article series, we take a second look at current events in countries that often remain only briefly spotlighted in German reporting. Together with local experts, we ask: What political and social developments lie behind the current events that we see in the news? What does this mean for democracy and media freedom? With our exile expertise, we want to reveal global connections and understand what we can learn from this for free, democratic coexistence. In this episode, Azerbaijani journalist Fatima Karimova writes about the repression of media workers in her homeland and why the European Union repeatedly turns a blind eye to it.

item.title: „White Gold“: Debris and Deception
item.description: Crooked deals with waste are just as lucrative to drug deals – only easier to conceal. An investigation by CORRECTIV.Europe shows how two companies from Germany and Czechia are making hundreds of thousands of tonnes of debris disappear just behind the border.

item.title: Russia declares CORRECTIV an “undesirable organization”
item.description: The Russian Prosecutor General's Office has designated CORRECTIV as an “undesirable foreign organization.” With this move, the Russian state is placing our journalistic work under blanket threat of punishment—while simultaneously demonstrating that our reporting is effective. Independent investigations are to be made impossible in Russia.

item.title: Despite sanctions: Putin‘s war waged with European machinery
item.description: Without machines from abroad, Russia’s weapons factories would grind to a halt. This analysis of Russian import data shows German and European companies supplied goods with potential dual-use applications over 28,000 times in the lead-up to the invasion. How this has impacted the war is often overlooked.

item.title: “Every minute, a building in Europe is destroyed”
item.description: The EU wants millions of old buildings to be renovated. But frequently the opposite happens: existing houses are demolished and replaced by new builds. Exactly how many buildings are being torn down remains a blind spot. CORRECTIV wants to close this gap in the data.

item.title: How Much European Real Estate is Owned by Russians? The EU has no Idea
item.description: Despite sweeping sanctions, Russian nationals can still legally purchase property in the EU. Several member states view this as a major security risk. Our investigation reveals how an EU-wide ban collapsed due to the resistance of a single country.

item.title: Where Europe is Dumping its Problematic Waste
item.description: In the middle of Europe, a contaminated legacy of the Soviet nuclear program has turned into a lucrative opportunity for the waste industry. Our investigation reveals that companies continue to dump millions of tons of old tyres, shoes, and even hazardous waste.

item.title: The Man Suing Trump
item.description: A Conversation with Ben Wizner, US Civil Rights Attorney

item.title: Demolition Atlas Europe launched: CORRECTIV investigates demolitions across Europe
item.description: Every year, hundreds of thousands of buildings are demolished across Europe. In cooperation with international media, we uncover the ecological, social and cultural consequences.

item.title: Where Travel Platforms like Airbnb have Transformed Europe’s Tourism
item.description: Short-term rentals through online platforms are surging – far outpacing traditional tourism. Using local-level data, CORRECTIV.Europe reveals for the first time where EU residents are confronted with especially high numbers of visitors.

item.title: Eleven football players report more than a hundred cases of intimate touching by a German player consultant
item.description: Research by CORRECTIV shows: The often underage young footballers, some of whom now play professional football, are said to have been treated naked in the counsellor's offices under the pretext of sports medicine treatment.

item.title: The Taliban’s Algorithmic Emirate: How bots can reinforce and shape a political system
item.description: How the Taliban use fake identities and bot accounts to simulate support – and exploit the digital space for their propaganda. An investigation into targeted manipulation, virtual control, and the threat to open societies.

item.title: “It’s difficult to explain that you freeze to death at 5 degrees Celsius”
item.description: An estimated 47 Million people in Europe cannot afford a warm home in winter, according to a calculation from CORRECTIV.Europe. Reports from local journalists in our network show the dimension of the problem in several countries.

item.title: “I’m always cold”
item.description: 47 million people in Europe cannot afford to heat their homes in winter, according to an analysis by CORRECTIV.Europe. Millions are also affected in Germany. Experts warn this may lead to social conflict.

item.title: EU states not prepared for new carbon pricing
item.description: Carbon pricing for transport and heating fuels is to be introduced across the EU from 2027. But several countries are now questioning the rapid phase-out of fossil fuels – which could mean even higher costs in the long term. “We are sleepwalking towards a political disaster,” social democratic MEP Thomas Pellerin-Carlin warns.

item.title: Influence operation exposed: How Russia meddles in Germany’s election campaign
item.description: A CORRECTIV investigation has uncovered that a Russian disinformation campaign established around 100 fake websites ahead of Germany’s general election. Their purpose: to influence the election campaign due to take place in February. In several cases, these sites have already been used to discredit German politicians.

item.title: Doppelganger: CORRECTIV investigations bring Russian propaganda campaign to a halt
item.description: The spread of fake websites by the Russian disinformation campaign Doppelganger has largely been stopped. The people behind the campaign had been using a Ukrainian service provider – which quickly blocked the Russian customer after a CORRECTIV inquiry. Doppelganger’s digital footprints meanwhile lead directly to the Ministry of Defense in Moscow.

item.title: Europe On Fire: How Rising Temperatures Are Threatening Energy Supply
item.description: Hotter summers pose a serious health risk. They also threaten the stability of energy supplies throughout Europe. CORRECTIV.Europe shows on a detailed map which regions are affected the most.

item.title: CORRECTIV.Europe with new leadership: Joanna Krawczyk becomes Managing Director, Frida Thurm strengthens the editorial team
item.description: The public interest non-profit media house CORRECTIV is advancing the restructuring of its European department CORRECTIV.Europe with international expertise: Joanna Krawczyk takes over as Managing Director of CORRECTIV.Europe as of October 1, 2024. With her extensive experience in the European media landscape and her commitment to independent journalism, she will drive the strategic development and execution of CORRECTIV.Europe forward.

item.title: CORRECTIV.Europe restructures, editor-in-chief Olaya Argüeso Pérez leaves CORRECTIV
item.description: The media house CORRECTIV is restructuring one of its core projects: CORRECTIV.Europe is to become an even stronger central hub for Europe's local editors, journalists and communities. As part of the restructuring of CORRECTIV.Europe, Olaya Argüeso Pérez is leaving CORRECTIV as Editor-in-Chief.

item.title: Inside Doppelganger – How Russia uses EU companies for its propaganda
item.description: For two years, Russia has been spreading its propaganda using cloned websites of Western media outlets. The campaign known as "Doppelganger" hasn’t been stopped yet – despite being sanctioned by the EU and US. A CORRECTIV investigation found that European companies are part of the internet infrastructure that keeps the campaign running.

item.title: In the Glass Palace – Abuse of Power and Sexual Harassment in the EU Parliament
item.description: Just weeks before the EU elections, a contentious issue is forcing its way onto the agenda behind the scenes at the European Parliament. Sexual assault and bullying within Parliament itself. Several dozen women and men have reported cases of unwanted touching, emotional abuse and physical violence to CORRECTIV and the German newspaper Stern—mostly by MEPs.

item.title: Hacks and Propaganda: Meet the Two Brothers Bringing Russia’s Cyber War to Europe
item.description: Since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Russia has stepped up disinformation and hacking campaigns against the West. A CORRECTIV investigation shows how two brothers from Moldova provide the technology needed for these attacks.

item.title: Don’t Bother Asking AI About the EU Elections: How Chatbots Fail When It Comes to Politics
item.description: We asked three of the best-known AI chatbots multiple questions on the upcoming EU elections and international politics. Our experiment shows: Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot and ChatGPT fail when it comes to answering political questions. They make false statements about candidates or fabricate sources. Depending on the language, the bots also provide very different answers.

item.title: The EU’s Long Road Towards Sustainable Agriculture
item.description: The EU has committed itself to become carbon-neutral by 2050. Farming plays a key role in that goal. However, the sector’s lobbying efforts have allowed large players to avoid stricter environmental controls.

item.title: The Green Gas Lie
item.description: German gas providers‘ claims about their “climate-neutral” natural gas are little more than greenwashing, CORRECTIV has revealed. The gas is linked to the deforestation of supposedly protected forests and the expansion of gas-fired power stations. We expose an industry deceiving hundreds of thousands of customers and fuelling the climate crisis.

item.title: Secret plan against Germany
item.description: It was the meeting that nobody was ever meant to find out about. Back in November, high-ranking politicians from Germany’s far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party, neo-Nazis, and sympathetic businesspeople gathered in a hotel near Potsdam. Their agenda? Nothing less than the fine tuning of a plan for the forced deportations of millions of people currently living in Germany.

item.title: How CORRECTIV’s journalism made a difference this year
item.description: The German government launches an investigation, a court takes the ex-pope to court and a sanction is imposed: CORRECTIV's research once again had direct impacts in 2023. We show what has changed for the better.

item.title: CORRECTIV is working on a new AI tool
item.description: In the JournalismAI Fellowship, CORRECTIV developed the prototype for a new AI application within an international team of editors and developers.

item.title: German rifles for Russia
item.description: Since the beginning of Russia's war in Ukraine more than 7000 rifles and more than 8 million shots of ammunition made by Western manufacturers made their way to Russia. Some of them are being used in the front lines. German manufacturers are affected, too – caused by sanction loopholes.

item.title: Industrial air pollution costs Europe 265 billion euros in one year
item.description: Europe's coal-fired power plants poison our air like no other industry. Giants such as PGE, RWE or Vattenfall emit tons of pollutants yearly, with harsh consequences for our health and the environment. The damage cost us billions of euros.

item.title: Alternative for Russia: How the AfD is systematically turning towards Russia
item.description: The German far-right political party Alternative for Germany (Alternative für Deutschland) has set its sights on Russia. Their election manifesto barely mentions the West or NATO. Provocative trips, aggressive political speeches and pro-Russian motions in the Bundestag (German parliament) all reveal a party whose foreign policy is pandering to Moscow.

item.title: Deforestation: German development bank is financing environmental destruction
item.description: Germany's national development bank DEG is funding dubious projects in the Global South. CORRECTIV and El Surtidor have been reporting on the deforestation crisis in Paraguay which is co-financed by the DEG. The German government is doing nothing about it.

item.title: Job posting: Freelance Developer Frontend / Backend
item.description: part time, freelance for 2 month, Berlin/Essen or remote

item.title: Politicians of Germany’s far-right AfD are benefitting from a pro-Russian propaganda campaign. Here is how.
item.description: A network of fake accounts on Facebook is agitating against Ukraine and has been sharing fake pro-Russian articles and websites for months. Politicians of the far-right party Alternative für Deutschland seem to also benefit: the network ran ads to promote content by the party’s politicians.

item.title: Facebook silent as pro-Kremlin disinformation campaign rages on
item.description: Despite Facebook’s supposed takedown last year, a pro-Russian disinformation campaign continues to be active on the social-media platform. It is promoting spoofed news and government websites, as well as content by politicians of Germany’s far-right AfD party.

item.title: Dirty pensions: Climate activists know nothing about their investments in gas and oil
item.description: Anyone who puts their money into pension funds risks profiting from climate-damaging corporations in Germany as well - unknowingly. An international and local investigation led by CORRECTIV reveals connections for the first time.

item.title: Chinese fraudsters systematically smuggle clothing into the EU
item.description: Chinese fraudsters smuggling masses of textiles into Europe are evading import fees. CORRECTIV research shows: The scam is costing the EU billions of euros. Customs cannot keep up with controls and member states are looking the other way.

item.title: Call for applications for illustrators – Graphic Novel on Community Investigation
item.description: The Seek Initiative in collaboration with CORRECTIV is looking for an illustrator for a graphic novel on the topic of community investigation. The illustrator will work closely with the team composed of the author, an illustrations coordinator at CORRECTIV and a point person at the Seek Initiative.

item.title: Vodka, Scholz and Gazprom
item.description:
Vodka, Scholz and Gazprom This is how young lobbyists celebrated good business with Russia – and fueled gas dependency. They really let their hair down: white rabbits, dirndls and Stalin doubles all made appearances during the festivities. Sponsored by a host of companies from Gazprom to Porsche, a new generation of German-Russian business lobbyists celebrated. […]

The post Vodka, Scholz and Gazprom appeared first on correctiv.org.

item.title: Devastating Supply Chains
item.description: The German federal government is lobbying in Brussels for a restriction of the liability rules in the EU Supply Chain Act – seemingly under pressure from the Free Democratic Party (FDP) and industry. This has been revealed by investigations by CORRECTIV and Frontal. The example of natural rubber shows how demand in Europe drives deforestation and displacement in Africa.

item.title: Charcoal: Somalia’s burning issue
item.description: In Somalia, terrorists and parts of the state profit from the charcoal trade, according to those involved – a trade which is harmful to both nature and the population

item.title: The Amazon machine
item.description: Amazon sends millions of parcels before Christmas in Germany. Powering the logistics giant is a system built on pressure and surveillance.

item.title: Forged government documents and fake news sites: Russian disinformation campaign targets Germany
item.description: A network of fake news sites has been flooding Europe with disinformation and propaganda against Ukraine for months. Reports uncovered websites that mimicked media outlets like Bild and Spiegel. But it doesn’t stop there. Research by CORRECTIV.Faktencheck shows that the Russian campaign also entails forged government documents.

item.title: Grand Theft Europe
item.description: Fraudsters are every year robbing Europe’s citizens of €50 billion in tax money. A Europe-wide investigation by 63 journalists from 30 countries, coordinated by CORRECTIV.

item.title: “With a few simple steps“: How RT DE circumvents the EU sanctions
item.description: In March the EU banned Russian broadcasters. Among them RT, formerly known as Russia Today. Since then, its German version RT DE has been advertising digital loopholes to work around its suspension. Above all: mirror pages, dozens of them. Why have the responsible German authorities not managed to shut them down?

item.title: The Heartland Lobby
item.description: An undercover investigation from CORRECTIV reveals how the American Heartland Institute is supporting climate change deniers in Germany with the goal of undermining climate protection measures.

item.title: The President and the Arms Dealer
item.description: A story of international arms deals – and expensive gifts in Berlin. A CORRECTIV investigation with public broadcaster ZDF’s Frontal21 and Stern magazine.

item.title: Flight MH17
item.description:
It’s one of the greatest war crimes of modern times – and the truth still hasn’t been told. On July 17th 2014 at about 16:20 local time, Malaysia Airlines flight MH17 was shot down over eastern Ukraine. All 298 passengers died, including many children. Who fired the missile? Over several months the Germany-based non-profit investigative […]

item.title: “The fight is the same”: How “Unser Mitteleuropa” is building a network of right-wing media in Europe
item.description: They stir up hatred against migration or spread misinformation: Media outlets from eleven European countries are cooperating to increase their influence. They are close to parties like the FPÖ, the AfD or Fratelli d’Italia. At the heart of it all: the website “Unser Mitteleuropa” (Our Central Europe) and a dead Austrian man with contacts to the right-wing extremist scene.

item.title: The Gazprom-Lobby
item.description: How Russia enlisted German politicians, business leaders and lawyers to ensure German dependence on Russian gas.

item.title: Monitoring Disinformation around Elections: Key Takeaways from the German Federal Elections in 2021
item.description: This report details the knowledge that CORRECTIV.Faktencheck has gained over five years of monitoring mis- and disinformation during elections. It highlights the 2021 federal elections in Germany and the key learnings that can be drawn from it. This includes the different tasks within the team, monitored platforms, tools, and thoughts behind the chosen approach.

item.title: Reports of sexual violence in the war: Why the Ukrainian parliament dismissed Human Rights Chief Denisova
item.description: The Ukrainian parliament dismissed Human Rights Chief Lyudmila Denisova amid claims that she spoke unethically about rape and sexual violence committed by Russian soldiers against Ukrainian civilians. Some German-language websites accuse her of inventing cases all together. What truth is there to these accusations?

item.title: Data analysis: users find questionable information on the coronavirus especially on Youtube and disseminate it via Whatsapp
item.description: CORRECTIV.Faktencheck has evaluated more than 1,800 reader submissions on possible disinformation about the coronavirus. The analysis shows that Whatsapp is the most common dissemination channel for questionable information – and Youtube is the place where it can be found. What are social media companies doing about it?
